## A. The paper's new subsections (paper_body.tex, FIVED16 blocks)

> \subsection{A sixteen-cell five-observable measurement}
> A five-observable cross section with total uncertainties is reported separately from those reporting definitions: configuration~(e)'s data result on 16 cells, R00--R15. They come from the 32 boxes formed by one interior edge per axis ($\pT$ 0.7, $\pPar$ 4.5~GeV/$c$, $\Eavail$ 0.8, $q_3$ 2, $W$ 1.8~GeV), of which the study's 27 coarser cells are the supported ones; each supported box with purity below 0.1 is merged into a neighbour, 4 boxes remain unreported, and every reported cell passes the support rule. Its model term differs from the study's envelope: there, the largest shift of a cell over five generator-sized truth changes, added linearly to the half-width; here, a covariance built from three generator shifts. The reported covariance is $C_{\mathrm{total}}+C_{\mathrm{resp}}$. $C_{\mathrm{total}}$ sums the statistical, flux, interaction, detector, lateral and normalization uncertainties of configuration~(e), a training-seed term measured to be zero, and $C_{\mathrm{model}}$. $C_{\mathrm{model}}$ is built from the change in the unfolded data when the prior is reweighted to GENIE + MEC, NuWro and GiBUU in turn; it is generator-shape model dependence, unscaled and not a calibrated bound, and its coverage at truths held out of its construction has not been validated. $C_{\mathrm{resp}}$ is the response of the result to a one-standard-deviation scale of the reconstructed recoil energy in the simulation, for protons, mesons, electromagnetic and other deposits; it does not cover neutron or muon deposits, nor species, energy-dependence or resolution effects beyond a scale, and it does not enter the generator tests of Sec.~\ref{sec:joint} or the paper's other results. The median per-cell relative uncertainty is 7.29\% (6.74\% without $C_{\mathrm{resp}}$). The note gives the cells, the central values, the per-group uncertainties and the correlation matrix of the reported covariance.
> To compare the estimator's bias with the reported covariance when the truth differs from the simulation, we unfold pseudo-data at 12 truths and compare the mean unfolded result with each truth on the 16 cells through $\chi^2$ with 16 degrees of freedom. The truths are the simulation's prior; the five hybrid truths of the generator tests of Sec.~\ref{sec:joint}, each a prediction on the fine grid; NuWro shape changes in $\Eavail$ and in $(\pT,\pPar,\Eavail)$; a GENIE + MEC shape change in $(\Eavail,W)$; a GiBUU-to-GENIE $\Eavail$ ratio; a noise-free closure at the NuWro shape; and a synthetic tilt of the $q_3$ distribution at fixed $(\Eavail,W)$. A truth from a generator that contributes to $C_{\mathrm{model}}$ is compared with the covariance without that generator's component, so that no such truth is compared with a covariance that includes its own generator's component; 6 further truths, whose offset correction failed its control, are ungraded and given in the note. A truth is listed when $p<0.01$ or when a cell has $|z|>2$. Table~\ref{tab:fd16} gives the results under the reported covariance and under $C_{\mathrm{total}}$ alone.
> Under the reported covariance, without the GiBUU component for the two GiBUU truths, the bias is listed at the GiBUU $\Eavail$ shape (cell R06, $z=2.01$), at the GiBUU hybrid truth ($p=8.0\times10^{-29}$; cells R02, R06, R07) and at the synthetic $q_3$ tilt ($p=6.4\times10^{-6}$): the reported uncertainty does not cover the fake-data bias at these GiBUU-like truths or at the $q_3$ tilt. At the other 9 truths the bias stays within the reported uncertainty by both criteria: no cell beyond $2\sigma$ and $p\geq0.01$.

> \subsection{Comparison on the sixteen reported cells}
> Table~\ref{tab:gen16} compares the sixteen-cell result of Sec.~\ref{sec:result16} with five predictions through $\chi^2$ against the reported covariance plus each prediction's finite-sample (diagonal) covariance $V_g$, with shape-only $\chi^2$ beside it; no diagonal-only $\chi^2$ is formed. Figure~\ref{fig:ratio16} shows the data over each prediction, cell by cell. GiBUU's sample stops at $E_\nu=20$~GeV, so it is compared on the 8 cells with $\pPar<4.5$~GeV/$c$ only. The reported uncertainty does not cover the fake-data bias at the GiBUU-like truths (Sec.~\ref{sec:result16}). NuWro and GiBUU are on carbon, with no correction to CH, and MINERvA Tune~v1 is the simulation's prior. Because $C_{\mathrm{model}}$ is built from shifts toward GENIE + MEC, NuWro and GiBUU, each relative to GENIE CV, those comparisons use a covariance built in part from the compared generator, and the GENIE CV comparison does through that reference.
> Weakening only the flux correlations by 10\,\% lowers the $\chi^2$ of the 16-cell predictions by 24--48\,\%. The same change to the detector or lateral correlations lowers it by at most 18\,\%. With the correlations of the interaction, flux, detector and lateral groups removed, every 16-cell prediction keeps $\chi^2\geq45$ for 16 degrees of freedom.

## B. The note's new chapter (sec_fived16.tex), prose only (tables in the PDF)

> \section{The sixteen-cell five-observable measurement}
> This section gives a five-dimensional cross-section result with total uncertainties: the data result of configuration~(e) (\S\ref{sec:method-config}) on 16 cells, R00--R15, with the reported covariance $C_{\mathrm{total}}+C_{\mathrm{resp}}$. It is a separate product from the configuration-(a) five-dimensional central value of Secs.~\ref{sec:eavailw} and~\ref{sec:5d} and from the five-axis covariance used with that central value (\S\ref{sec:eavailw-adopted}). Statements in those sections about that central value and that covariance do not describe this result, and statements here do not describe them. The section gives the cells and the result (\S\ref{sec:fived16-result}), the covariance and what it is built from (\S\ref{sec:fived16-cov}), the fake-data tests of the estimator's bias against the covariance (\S\ref{sec:fived16-fd}) and the comparison with generator predictions (\S\ref{sec:fived16-gen}).
> \subsection{Cells and result}
> The cells are those of the H2 grid of \S\ref{sec:gbdt-model-dependence} after a purity merge. H2 divides each axis once, giving 32 boxes, with edges $\pT=(0, 0.7, 4.5)$, $\pPar=(1.5, 4.5, 60)$, $\Eavail=(0, 0.8, 100)$, $q_3=(0, 2, 100)$ and $W=(0, 1.8, 100)$, in the units of App.~\ref{sec:gbdt-diagnostic-definitions}; 27 of them pass that appendix's support rule. Each supported box whose purity is below $\tau=0.1$ is merged into a neighbour, in 12 declared steps; 1 unsupported box is absorbed into R09 by these merges, the other 4 remain unreported, and each of the 16 resulting cells passes the support rule. Table~\ref{tab:fived16-cells} gives each cell's box, its cell-integrated cross section $f$ and its relative uncertainty.
> \subsection{The reported covariance}
> The reported covariance is $C_{\mathrm{total}}+C_{\mathrm{resp}}$, with $C_{\mathrm{total}}=C_{\mathrm{e}}+C_{\mathrm{model}}$. $C_{\mathrm{e}}$ sums the statistical bootstrap of configuration~(e), the flux universes weighted by the neutrino--electron and inverse-muon-decay constraint, the interaction and detector bands, the lateral bands, the normalization and the training-seed block. The training-seed block was measured and is zero in every cell: with full-sample binning and deterministic training, the unfolds at the other seeds are bitwise equal to the central one. Table~\ref{tab:fived16-groups} gives each group's per-cell relative $\sigma$.
> $C_{\mathrm{model}}$ is built from the change in the unfolded data when the prior is reweighted to each of three generators, GENIE + MEC, NuWro and GiBUU: each vertex is that relative shift of the data result, and $C_{\mathrm{model}}$ is the sum of their outer products, unscaled. It is generator-shape model dependence, not a calibrated bound. Its coverage at truths held out of its construction has not been validated. GiBUU's shape is applied only below $\pPar=10$~GeV/$c$, above which the prior is unchanged; between $\pPar=6$ and 10~GeV/$c$ GiBUU's sample lacks the part above $E_\nu=20$~GeV: at least 4.9--5.3\% of the cross section there, from GENIE CV and NuWro samples that stop at $E_\nu=50$~GeV. GiBUU's vertex carries 0.890 of $C_{\mathrm{model}}$'s trace, NuWro's 0.095 and GENIE + MEC's 0.014. In every cell, 77--100\% of the prior weight lies beside a step in the reweighting ratio larger than 0.1 drawn by the noise gate or a cut, and the shifts enter as measured.
> $C_{\mathrm{resp}}$ is the response of configuration~(e)'s data result to a one-standard-deviation scale of the simulation's reconstructed recoil energy, for protons, mesons, electromagnetic deposits and other deposits separately, summed over the four. It does not cover neutron or muon deposits, the effects of particle species, energy dependence and resolution beyond a scale, the null distributions of the joint tests, the configuration-(a) products or the two-, three- and four-dimensional results. A cross-talk term, reported beside $C_{\mathrm{resp}}$ and not summed into it, has a median per-cell relative $\sigma$ of 0.36\%. Its median per-cell relative $\sigma$ is 2.14\%, and adding it raises the total's $\sigma$ by a factor of 1.011--1.220 (median 1.048). Of the trace of $(C_{\mathrm{total}}+C_{\mathrm{resp}})/f f^{T}$, $C_{\mathrm{total}}$ carries 0.9262 and the four response species 0.0168, 0.0436, 0.0071 and 0.0062.
> Table~\ref{tab:fived16-corr} gives the correlation matrix of $C_{\mathrm{total}}+C_{\mathrm{resp}}$; with the central values and the relative uncertainties of Table~\ref{tab:fived16-cells}, it gives the reported covariance to the printed precision.
> \subsection{Fake-data tests of the estimator's bias}
> The fake-data tests ask how the estimator's bias at a truth different from the simulation compares with the reported covariance. Pseudo-data are generated at 12 graded truths and unfolded with configuration~(e), and the mean unfolded result is compared with each truth on the 16 cells, through $\chi^2$ with 16 degrees of freedom and the per-cell pull $z$. The truths are the simulation's prior; the five hybrid truths of the generator tests (Sec.~\ref{sec:joint5d}), each a prediction on the fine grid; the historical shapes W1, W2 and W3 of \S\ref{sec:gbdt-model-dependence}; a GiBUU-to-GENIE $\Eavail$ shape; a noise-free closure at the NuWro shape; and a synthetic tilt of the $q_3$ distribution at fixed $(\Eavail,W)$. A truth from a generator that contributes a vertex to $C_{\mathrm{model}}$ is compared with the covariance without that vertex, so that no such truth is compared with a covariance that contains its own generator's shift. A truth is listed when $p<0.01$, or when a cell has $|z|>2$. These are not held-out truths, and the detector response is not probed. Table~\ref{tab:fived16-fd} gives each truth under the reported covariance and, beside it, under $C_{\mathrm{total}}$ alone.
> Measured against the reported covariance, without the vertex of the truth's own generator where one exists, 3 truths are listed: the GiBUU $\Eavail$ shape, by its cell R06 ($z=2.01$); the GiBUU hybrid truth, by $p$ and by its cells R02, R06, R07; and the $q_3$ tilt, by $p$ ($p=6.4\times10^{-6}$). The reported uncertainty does not cover the fake-data bias at these GiBUU-like truths or at the $q_3$ tilt. At the other 9 truths the bias stays within the reported uncertainty by both criteria: no cell beyond $2\sigma$ and $p\geq0.01$.
> The counts are read by group, never pooled. The vertex-family truths are the 8 from GENIE + MEC, NuWro or GiBUU, each compared without its vertex; the non-vertex truths are the GENIE CV hybrid and the $q_3$ tilt; the prior truths are the simulation prior and the Tune~v1 hybrid. Under the reported covariance, the vertex-family truths have 4 of 128 cells with $|z|>2$ (Gaussian reference 5.82) and 1 of 8 truths with $p<0.01$ (reference 0.08); the non-vertex truths 0 of 32 and 1 of 2; and the prior truths 0 of 32 and 0 of 2. The references are context only, because the bias is deterministic.
> Controls 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 passed. The offset control, which compares two hybrid truths' offset corrections, failed ($\chi^2=245.74$ for 16 degrees of freedom). As declared, the six power alternatives built on that correction are therefore descriptive and ungraded; Table~\ref{tab:fived16-fdvar} gives them, with the two descriptive variants of each graded truth.
> \subsection{Comparison with generator predictions}
> Table~\ref{tab:fived16-gen} compares the result with five predictions through $\chi^2$ against the reported covariance plus each prediction's finite-sample (diagonal) covariance $V_g$, $C_{\mathrm{total}}+C_{\mathrm{resp}}+V_g$, with its number of degrees of freedom, and through the shape-only $\chi^2$, which frees the normalization. No diagonal-only $\chi^2$ is formed. GiBUU's sample has no events above $E_\nu=20$~GeV, so it is compared on the 8 cells below $\pPar=4.5$~GeV/$c$ only, and no value is formed on the other 8. In the GENIE CV and NuWro samples, which stop at $E_\nu=50$~GeV, at least 11.71\% and 12.59\% of each generator's cross section in the phase space above $\pPar=4.5$~GeV/$c$ comes from $E_\nu>20$~GeV, against 0.83\% and 0.77\% between $\pPar=1.5$ and 4.5~GeV/$c$: these are the parts that a sample stopping at $E_\nu=20$~GeV cannot hold, not GiBUU numbers. The NuWro and GiBUU predictions are on a carbon target, with no correction to CH. MINERvA Tune~v1 is the simulation's prior, not an independent prediction. Each $C_{\mathrm{model}}$ vertex is a data shift unfolded with a prior reweighted by one generator's ratio to GENIE CV, so the GENIE + MEC, NuWro and GiBUU comparisons each use a covariance built in part from the compared generator, and the GENIE CV comparison does through the ratios' reference.
> The variant without the response block, against $C_{\mathrm{total}}+V_g$, gives $\chi^2$ of 160.62/16, 318.26/16, 298.69/16, 68.44/8 and 360.79/16, in the order of Table~\ref{tab:fived16-gen}. Table~\ref{tab:fived16-pulls} gives each cell's pull and $(g-f)/f$.
> The fake-data tests list the GiBUU-like truths under the reported covariance (\S\ref{sec:fived16-fd}), so the GiBUU comparison carries that limitation.
> Weakening only the flux correlations by 10\,\% lowers the $\chi^2$ of the 16-cell predictions by 24--48\,\%. The same change to the detector or lateral correlations lowers it by at most 18\,\%. With the correlations of the interaction, flux, detector and lateral groups removed, every 16-cell prediction keeps $\chi^2\geq45$ for 16 degrees of freedom. Table~\ref{tab:fived16-sens} gives each group's sensitivity, GiBUU's eight-cell values included. These are descriptive sensitivities of the reported $\chi^2$, not alternative results: one group's correlations are shrunk toward the diagonal by a fraction $\alpha$ of the way, with its variances kept.
> The $\chi^2$ can be decomposed along the eigenmodes of each prediction's matrix (Table~\ref{tab:fived16-diag}). The decomposition is a breakdown, not an alternative result; a mode is that matrix's own, and its dominant block is the covariance group with the largest share of its variance. Figure~\ref{fig:fived16-modes} shows, for each sixteen-cell prediction, the three modes that carry most of its $\chi^2$ and the prediction's distance along each.
> Cell R04 ($\pT<0.7$, $\pPar\geq4.5$, $\Eavail<0.8$, $q_3<2$) has the smallest relative $\sigma$ of the sixteen, 4.20\,\%, of which flux is the largest group at 3.47\,\%. Under the flux block alone its correlation with the 7 cells that load with it in the top modes is 0.972--0.998; under the reported covariance it is 0.40--0.81.

### app_negweight.tex (7)

- The 2D result and its covariance, the 3D and 4D central values and the sixteen-cell five-dimensional result (\S\ref{sec:fived16}) use its refined form (\S\ref{sec:method-algo}); binned purity remains the treatment of the configuration-(a) five-dimensional central value and its five-axis covariance and of the extended-fiducial value.
- \paragraph{The standard \(N\)-dimensional chain uses purity.} The entire standard five-dimensional chain, that of the configuration-(a) central value and its five-axis covariance, uses binned purity (\S\ref{sec:method-algo}): the central unfold, $169$ vertical-band unfolds, $18$ detector unfolds and $10$ endpoint unfolds of the re-selected lateral bands.
- For the configuration-(a) five-dimensional central value, which still uses purity, the revisit is open; the sixteen-cell result (\S\ref{sec:fived16}) uses the refined estimator.
- That estimator is configuration (e), which gives the 3D and 4D central values and the sixteen-cell result (\S\ref{sec:fived16}) but not the configuration-(a) 5D central value; the quoted 2D central value uses the same refinement capacity, in configuration (f).
- The within-bin shape term of \S\ref{sec:negweight-estimator} is therefore measurable, and it is direct evidence for revisiting the background treatment of the configuration-(a) five-dimensional central value (\S\ref{sec:negweight-footing}).
- Reducing one bias does not itself qualify an uncertainty, so this result does not close the revisit of the background treatment of the configuration-(a) five-dimensional central value (\S\ref{sec:negweight-footing}).
- The lateral-band component from re-selected event loops is built, with five bands and ten endpoint unfolds whose distinct checksums are listed in the record of the five-axis covariance of the configuration-(a) central value.

- The sixteen-cell result also has total uncertainties, whose coverage is not validated; Sec.~\ref{sec:result16} gives the fake-data study's measured comparison of the estimator's bias with its reported covariance.

### sec_5d.tex (14)

- \section{Five-dimensional estimator: validation and uncertainty} \label{sec:5d} This section gives the validation of the five-dimensional estimator behind the central values of \S\S\ref{sec:3d}--\ref{sec:eavailw}: what each validation test isolates (\S\ref{sec:val-fiveaxis}), background subtraction and generator-sized truth changes (\S\ref{sec:val-negweight}), why the estimator does not follow such changes (\S\ref{sec:val-departure}), model dependence and the reporting definitions it rules out (\S\ref{sec:gbdt-model-dependence}), the five-dimensional coverage test (\S\ref{sec:coverage-5d}), and the status of the five-axis covariance of the configuration-(a) central value (\S\ref{sec:eavailw-construction}).
- The sixteen-cell result of configuration (e) follows in \S\ref{sec:fived16}, and the calibrated generator tests built on a variant of this estimator in \S\ref{sec:joint5d}.

- Relative to these cells' total uncertainty in the configuration-(a) covariance, the bias is 0.36--1.07 standard deviations.
- Negative-weight subtraction is not used for the configuration-(a) five-dimensional central value; the sixteen-cell result uses it (\S\ref{sec:fived16}).
- The $\Eavail$ and $q_3$ residuals, a regularization (unfolding-model) bias of the estimator, enter no uncertainty quoted for the configuration-(a) central value.
- For the sixteen-cell result (\S\ref{sec:fived16}), the model term of its reported covariance is the change in the unfolded data when the prior is reweighted to each generator (GENIE + MEC, NuWro, GiBUU; \S\ref{sec:fived16-cov}), unscaled and not a calibrated bound; \S\ref{sec:fived16-fd} gives the fake-data study's measured comparison of the estimator's bias with the reported covariance.
- \paragraph{Unfolding-model dependence.} For historical shapes held out while this candidate was assessed (NuWro; GENIE with enhanced meson-exchange currents), its unfolding-model dependence is median \SIrange{2}{6}{\percent} and at most \SIrange{16}{31}{\percent}, within the configuration-(a) total uncertainty in 20 of the 42 $(\Eavail,W)$ cells.
- This candidate is configuration (e), which gives the sixteen-cell result (\S\ref{sec:fived16}); no uncertainty from this assessment is used for a quoted result.
- With the study's precision targets and computing budget, none of its reporting definitions (RD1--RD3, next paragraph) met a precision target.
- The sixteen-cell result is reported on the same H2 grid after a purity merge of its supported boxes, with total uncertainties (\S\ref{sec:fived16-result}).
- \paragraph{Reporting definitions for a five-dimensional measurement.} The five-dimensional precision study assessed three reporting definitions at the development resolution: the 109 J cells (RD1), the 27 H2 cells (RD2) and the 39 EW cells (RD3).
- None of the three reporting definitions can meet these precision targets with any estimator configuration the study's selection procedure permits within its computing budget.
- \subsection{The five-axis covariance of the configuration-(a) central value and its $(\Eavail,W)$ projection} \label{sec:eavailw-construction} \paragraph{Status.} \label{sec:eavailw-adopted} The five-axis covariance used in this note is the variant centered on the central value (\texttt{cv}); its $(\Eavail,W)$ projection has \zprojCells\ cells.

### sec_eavailw.tex (2)

- The configuration-(a) five-dimensional unfolding in $(\pT,\pPar,\Eavail,q_{3},W)$ passes the marginalization checks against the lower-dimensional results: integrating over $W$ recovers the configuration-(a) 4D normalization to \SI{\eavailMargin}{\percent} (5D/4D total $=1.0011$), with median differences of \SIrange{0.3}{1.5}{\percent} per axis, and $d\sigma/dW$ is finite and non-negative in all six bins.
- These are central-value ratios; no compatibility metric based on the configuration-(a) covariance is quoted, for the reason given in \S\ref{sec:eavailw-adopted}, item~1 (comparison on the sixteen cells: \S\ref{sec:fived16-gen}).

### sec_method.tex (6)

- The quoted 2D result and its covariance, the 3D and 4D central values and the sixteen-cell 5D result and its covariance (\S\ref{sec:fived16}) use its refined form; every other quoted cross section and uncertainty, including the configuration-(a) 5D central value and the extended-fiducial value, uses the binned correction.
- The refined form is the background treatment of configurations (d), (e) and (f) (\S\ref{sec:method-config}): (d) in the background-bias and generator-sized-change studies of \S\ref{sec:val-negweight}; (e), the joint-test estimator, in \S\S\ref{sec:val-departure}--\ref{sec:gbdt-model-dependence}, the generator tests, the 3D and 4D central values and the sixteen-cell result; and (f) for the 2D result and its covariance (App.~\ref{app:negweight}, \S\ref{sec:3d}, \S\ref{sec:results}).
- It gives the 3D and 4D central values (\S\ref{sec:3d}) and the sixteen-cell five-dimensional result (\S\ref{sec:fived16}).
- The five-dimensional central value of \S\ref{sec:eavailw} and its five-axis covariance use configuration~(a): they were produced before the purity bias was found and the refinement was developed.
- A refined five-dimensional data unfold exists (configuration~(e)); it gives the sixteen-cell result, whose reported covariance on the sixteen cells is described in \S\ref{sec:fived16-cov}.

### sec_summary.tex (10)

- The regularization bias measured in \S\ref{sec:5d} is largest in the high-$\Eavail$, high-$W$ region (\S\ref{sec:eavailw-map}).
- The configuration-(a) five-dimensional central value keeps this bias, and no uncertainty quoted for it includes the bias.
- The refined negative-weight subtraction, which the sixteen-cell result uses (\S\ref{sec:fived16}), largely removes it.
- No uncertainty quoted for the configuration-(a) central value includes this residual bias, which is interpreted as regularization bias (\S\ref{sec:val-departure}).
- For the sixteen-cell result (\S\ref{sec:fived16}), the model term of its reported covariance is the change in the unfolded data when the prior is reweighted to each generator (GENIE + MEC, NuWro, GiBUU; \S\ref{sec:fived16-cov}), unscaled and not a calibrated bound; \S\ref{sec:fived16-fd} gives the fake-data study's measured comparison of the estimator's bias with the reported covariance, and its limitation.
- Above two dimensions the results are central values without intervals of validated coverage; the sixteen-cell result also has total uncertainties, whose coverage is not validated (\S\ref{sec:fived16}).
- None of the precision study's reporting definitions (RD1--RD3) met a precision target (\S\ref{sec:gbdt-model-dependence}); the sixteen-cell result is reported on the precision study's H2 grid after a purity merge of its supported boxes (\S\ref{sec:fived16-result}).
- The five-axis covariance of the configuration-(a) central value does not meet its specification's acceptance criteria.
- Two companion covariances, built at different estimator seeds, show a seed sensitivity above the limit set before production, so no significance based on the configuration-(a) covariance is quoted (\S\ref{sec:eavailw-adopted}; the comparison on the sixteen cells: \S\ref{sec:fived16-gen}).
- The release design and its public example have no bearing on the choice of the five-axis covariance of the configuration-(a) central value (\S\ref{sec:eavailw-adopted}).

### sec_systematics.tex (7)

- The configuration-(a) 5D result uses the strict joint ensemble and matched-endpoint comparator.
- In the five-axis covariance of the configuration-(a) central value the per-source decomposition is retained for attribution, and the joint throws enter through the inflation of Eq.~\eqref{eq:zinflation} (\S\ref{sec:eavailw-construction}).
- For the five kinematic bands (BeamAngleX/Y, MuonResolution, and Muon\_Energy\_MINERvA/MINOS), the re-selected event loops supply the lateral-band block of the five-axis covariance of the configuration-(a) central value; higher-dimensional products built from the single-pass shifted observables are not used for any quoted uncertainty.
- The ML term $C_{\mathrm{ML}}$ of the five-axis covariance of the configuration-(a) central value (Eq.~\eqref{eq:zassembly}) is the split-varied band: its ensemble fixes the estimator seed at 42 and varies the train/test split seed.
- The five-axis covariance of the configuration-(a) central value is a separate, later build in which the unified-throw covariance is centered on the central value (the CV-centered variant, \texttt{cv}; \S\ref{sec:eavailw-construction}).
- Per-universe background subtraction in all 187 universe unfolds and the CV changes the combined \emph{block-sum} sqrt-trace by only \SI{0.28}{\percent} and the five-axis covariance \emph{of the configuration-(a) central value} by \SI{0.18}{\percent}, a numerically negligible bound on the background-CV choice (Ref.~\cite{NoteRecords2026}, superseded values).
- The 4D and extended-fiducial results have no covariance from this procedure, and the configuration-(a) 5D covariance is not transferred to them.

- Signal only \\ \addlinespace Background-inclusive & Adds background simulation and rebuilds purity weights; nominal truth & 5D & Highest-$W$ column \SIrange{3.5}{4.1}{\percent} low; negative-weight treatment \SIrange{0.11}{0.24}{\percent}, with joint cells \SIrange{0.7}{1.1}{\percent} high (\S\ref{sec:val-negweight}) \\ \addlinespace Generator-shaped & Truth reweighted by GiBUU/GENIE ratio in $\Eavail$ (0.70--1.33 per bin) & 5D & Joint $(\Eavail,W)$ residuals median \SI{9.7}{\percent}, up to \SI{74}{\percent} at highest $W$; regularization bias outside every uncertainty quoted for the configuration-(a) central value (sixteen-cell result: \S\S\ref{sec:fived16-cov}, \ref{sec:fived16-fd}) \\ \addlinespace Withheld generator shapes & NuWro/GENIE and GENIE MEC/CV ratios & 5D & Median \SIrange{2}{6}{\percent}, at most \SIrange{16}{31}{\percent} per joint cell; within the configuration-(a) total uncertainty in 20 of 42 $(\Eavail,W)$ cells (\S\ref{sec:val-departure}) \\ \addlinespace Hidden $q_3$ & $q_3$ at fixed $(\Eavail,W)$ truth, amplitude 0.3 & 5D & $(\Eavail,W)$ cells shift by up to \SI{37}{\percent} \\ \addlinespace Response mismatch & Reconstructed $\Eavail$ of pseudo-data scaled & 5D & Protocol implemented, not run (App.~\ref{app:response-mismatch}) \\ \bottomrule \end{longtable} \paragraph{Why injected bumps close while generator-shaped tests do not.} The closing tests and the failing tests measure different things, so they do not contradict each other.
